title: Multiplexed crossbar lane scheduler for asymmetric burst overlap across heterogeneous GPUs
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Background: On heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters we observe a mismatch between short high-priority decode bursts and long prefill windows. Current rendezvous/NCCL-driven overlap strategies optimize for uniform token waves and tend to create either wasted bandwidth during sparse bursts or head-of-line latency for latency-sensitive requests. Goal: design and implement a multiplexed crossbar lane scheduler that dynamically partitions inter-GPU communication into fast lanes (low-latency, small-buffer bursts) and bulk lanes (high-throughput, larger coalesced transfers), with adaptive kernel selection hints so compute kernels and communication overlap more effectively across tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages.

Core idea: Introduce ephemeral lanes that are negotiated at per-request prefill time. Each lane carries a lane descriptor (priority, expected tokens, preferred kernel profile). The crossbar scheduler steers NCCL calls into per-lane streams that can be coalesced or isolated depending on current link utilization and lane latency SLOs. The runtime augments the kernel-selection path to emit lane-aware kernel preferences (fusion/no-fusion, attention tiling) so compute and comm can align (e.g., smaller attention tiles for fast-lane prefill to reduce stall time).

Key responsibilities:
- Admission control for fast lanes (protect p95 latency).
- Dynamic aggregation for bulk lanes (maximize tokens/sec).
- NCCL stream multiplexing: tagging collective ops and coalescing based on lane affinity.
- Kernel-selection hints API: lightweight metadata exchanged between scheduler and executor.
- Fall-back policy: if NCCL overlap fails or bandwidth saturates, automatically collapse fast lane into bulk with degraded SLO and emit an event.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs observability: lane multiplexing introduces tagging overhead; we add per-request trace tags and aggregate metrics to keep visibility.
- Fairness vs SLO guarantees: reserving capacity for fast lanes improves latency for some requests at throughput cost; we will expose config knobs per-customer and per-tier.
- Kernel fragmentation: more kernel variants increase binary surface; we will prioritize a small set of lane-aware kernels initially (2 variants) and fallback to generic kernels when needed.

Success metrics:
- p95 decode latency reduction for latency-tier requests >= 15% in mixed workloads.
- Aggregate throughput degradation <= 6% for heavy-bulk workloads.
- NCCL bandwidth utilization smoothing (reduction in variance) by >= 20%.
- Reduction in scheduler backpressure events on critical path.

Testing & experiments:
- Microbench harness for synthetic mixed workloads (latency-heavy tail + bulk prefill).
- Replay tests using production traces from last incident (prod-trace-2026-01-11).
- Canaries in Dedicated cluster with 2 availability zones, focus on heterogeneous GPU mixes (A100x2 + H100x1).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged runtime in staging; perf flags off by default.
2) Internal canary on small Dedicated pool (runtime-2.7-canary) with dark-launch metrics.
3) Gradual enable for low-volume customers using config knob 'lane_policy=conservative'.
4) Full enable for latency-tier customers after meeting SLO gates.

Observability additions:
- Per-lane metrics: lane_id, tokens_transferred, avg_latency, 95th_latency, nccL_coalesces, fallback_count.
- Dashboard: lane-overlap view and NCCL stream heatmap (linked below).
- Alerts: spike in fallback_count or lane admission rejections.

Risks & mitigations:
- Regression in throughput: limit fast lane admission and tune aggregation window.
- NCCL behavior variance across driver versions: add driver/version detection and compatibility matrix.
- Debugging complexity: add deterministic replay for lane assignment decisions.
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed - validated that tagging NCCL collectives with lane ids adds <0.6% extra CPU overhead in the orchestrator and negligible latency at kernel launch path.

2026-02-25: Prototype implemented: per-request lane descriptor pushed from prefill negotiator to RPC layer; NCCL wrapper now accepts lane_tag metadata. Experiment harness prepared (perf-harness/lane_v1).

2026-03-02: Microbench results: mixed workload (70% bulk, 30% latency) shows p95 decode latency improvement of 18% for fast-lane requests; aggregate tokens/sec dropped 3.7% compared to baseline. Attached more detailed numbers in attachments.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and runtime team. Decision: default fast-lane admission threshold set to 12 concurrent fast lanes per GPU for stable clusters. Action: add backpressure metric and per-GPU lane quota enforcement (ENG-874006 will track quota enforcement refactor).
2026-03-09: Safety net added: when fallback_count > 5 in 1m window, scheduler disables new fast lanes and triggers auto-rollout to bulk coalescing. This is under a feature flag 'lane_autosafety'.
2026-03-12: Preparing canary build: runtime-2.7-canary. PR opened for kernel hints path and NCCL tagging wrapper. See PR link in attachments.
comments: Marcus Patel (assignee): Need to ensure kernel cache invalidation won't blow up with extra kernel variants. Plan: keep variant count to 2 and reuse existing kernel cache buckets.
Alice Moreno (pm): Love the lane concept. Please add customer-configurable flavor: 'latency_strict' vs 'balanced'.
Rahul Singh (infra): We should capture per-GPU PCIe/NVLink utilization to feed admission control. Will add probe in infra-agent.
